messages:
tara: Heads-up — I landed a new synthetic harness for KV-cache long-context runs and I’m seeing steady memory creep after ~45m on our baseline. Repro steps and config below. Can folks help triage?

liam: thanks for the ping. can you paste the exact command you used?

tara: sure — run from eng-runtime/tools/kvbench: `./kvbench --workload long-context --clients 8 --seq-dist zipf --max-len 32768 --runtime 3600 --enable-prefix-cache`

alex: quick question: is this using the new continuous-batching kernel selection or the fallback path?

tara: kernel selection = auto (runtime picks optimized kernels). I forced `--kernel=continuous` and still saw the drift, slightly smaller slope but persists.

sasha: any heap/profile snapshots? metric I want: retained extents over time + fragment count.

tara: uploaded pprof and flamegraph to the artifacts bucket: gs://redwood-perf/kvcache/2312345678/ (heap-60m.pb.gz, flame-90m.svg). TL;DR: retained bytes climb ~12MB/hour after warmup, fragmentation edges up in same window.

liam: looked at flamegraph — hotspots around `kv::slot_alloc` and `kv::evict_page` paths, a decent chunk in the refcounting slowpath. Could be sticky refs preventing reuse.

perf-bot: regress-run summary: baseline (master@a1b2c3) vs experiment (your branch). Max RSS delta: +480MB after 1h. Regression flagged (severity: medium).

alex: do we have any long-running eviction tests in CI that exercise weird interleaving? Most ci jobs are 120s so they miss long-horizon effects.

tara: yea that's the point — I created this harness to surface slow leaks that only show under long contexts and interleaved reads/writes. I ran a 6h job with 32 clients and saw same pattern.

liam: I can run a repro locally with `--trace-kv` to dump per-slot last-touch timestamps and eviction counts. That should reveal if LRU aging isn't being updated correctly under continuous batching.

alex: also suspect our batching heuristics: if batch coalescing delays KV-touch updates into the kernel, we might miss updating the slot's LRU epoch. Two paths: update on host before dispatch or in kernel. Which do we currently do?

tara: currently we update LRU epoch on the host path, but only when `touch` events are synchronous — asynchronous kernel offload batches `touch` calls and applies them as a vector op. There may be race/ordering weirdness with evict decisions.

sasha: propose small experiment: 1) run with `--disable-async-touch` (host applies touch eagerly) 2) run with `--kv-compact-on-evict` enabled (aggressive reuse) 3) run with `--kernel=fallback` to isolate kernel path. Compare retained bytes.

tara: ran experiment 1 and 3 overnight: `--disable-async-touch` completely eliminated the slope in a 2h run (RSS stable). `--kernel=fallback` reduced slope but didn't eliminate. So async-touch batching is suspect.

liam: good repro signal. Next: add small logging around batched-touch apply to ensure we maintain ordering with eviction decisions. Could be that apply path drops entries when under pressure.

perf-bot: traced batch apply: some dropped ops seen when apply queue length > 8192 — backpressure metric fires, ops deferred.

alex: that backpressure threshold was tuned for latency — we possibly set it too low for long-tail workloads. If ops are deferred for too long, touch isn't applied and LRU thinks slot is cold => evicted => later reused and reallocated causing fragmentation.

sasha: recommended short-term mitigation: increase apply queue threshold to 65536 for long-context tests and add a test variant in synthetic harness that toggles it. Longer-term: make touch updates idempotent and resilient to reordering (store monotonic epoch on slot and ignore stale updates).

tara: created a PR draft with two changes: bump queue threshold behind a feature flag `kv_async_touch_queue=65536` and add monotonic epoch check in apply path. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/kvcache/pulls/4821 (WIP).

liam: nice. Also add a regression test in eng-runtime perf suite: job `kvcache_longrun_smoke` that runs harness for 2h on canary infra and asserts no >200MB RSS drift.

alex: note for CI: we should classify this test as nightly/canary only — cost too high for per-PR. But make it runnable locally for devs.

sasha: I'll write the test under eng-runtime/perf/jobs and wire the artifact uploader to capture pprof if RSS delta > 100MB.

tara: action items summarized: 
- liam: add tracing/logging around batched-touch apply (small PR)
- alex: gate and tune queue threshold; help with PR review
- sasha: add canary regression job + artifact capture
- tara: finish PR with monotonic epoch guard + unit tests

liam: I'll also simulate heavy interleaving with the fuzz harness to check for corner cases (concurrent evict+touch).

tara: thanks all — I’ll keep the artifacts live and post updates here. If you want to reproduce quickly: `./kvbench --workload long-context --clients 8 --runtime 7200 --enable-prefix-cache --trace-kv --kv_async_touch_queue=8192`

alex: noted. :+1:

sasha: adding this thread to the perf epic: KV-Longrun-2026 so we don't lose it.

perf-bot: job registered: eng-runtime/kvcache_longrun_smoke (cron: nightly-canary).
